quickPlayAnalysis.status: Cause not attributed: the Editor log of that session was overwritten and the phone has no log.
codeFacts: QuantumMenuUIMain.OnPlayButtonPressed sets ConnectionArgs.Region to PreferredRegion, empty by default, so the menu's FixedRegion override is empty and each client selects its own best region by ping (game/Assets/Photon/QuantumMenu/Runtime/QuantumMenuUIMain.cs and QuantumMenuConnectionBehaviourSDK.cs).

The party flow encodes the region index into the session code and decodes it on join, so both clients are forced into one region (QuantumMenuUIParty.cs, QuantumMenuPartyCodeGenerator.EncodeRegion and DecodeRegion).
Quick Play uses JoinRandomOrCreateRoom with ExpectedMaxPlayers equal to the client's MaxPlayers (game/Assets/Photon/PhotonRealtime/Code/MatchmakingExtensions.cs, BuildJoinRandomRoomArgs).
AppVersion is the menu machine id on both clients; a mismatch would also have broken the party code join, which worked.
candidates: Different best region on the two clients (most likely given the code path and the few seconds between presses).
Both clients creating a room before either was listed (race window of a few seconds).
Different MaxPlayers saved in the Editor's menu settings.
quickPlayAnalysis.productConsequence: The final lobby should pin one region for matchmaking while the player population is small; matchmaking will be driven by the game backend, not by the sample menu.

limits: Qualitative report only: no frame time, simulation time, memory or ping was recorded.
Six heroes only: no minions, towers or MOBA objectives, so this is not the representative 3v3 load defined in docs/PHOTON-ARCHITECTURE-AUDIT.md section 7.
Exact phone model, Chrome version and session length not recorded; 'Redmi 11C' is not a released model name.
No disconnection or reconnection was tested; PlayerTtlInSeconds is 0, so a dropped client cannot rejoin its slot.
